entry.title: I built a free PDF editor that never uploads your files
entry.summary: Most PDF tools ask for the same trade-off: upload your document to someone else's server, create an account, and hope a paywall does not appear halfway through. That is a problem when the file is a contract, a resume, a medical form, or anything else you would rather not send anywhere. I built TheEditPDF to remove that trade-off. It is a collection of 34 free PDF tools that run entirely in your browser. Your files are processed on your device, so nothing is uploaded. There is no signup, nothing to install, and no watermark. You can edit a PDF, add text, images, links and signatures, merge or split files, compress a large PDF, delete or rotate pages, protect a file with a password, redact sensitive text, and convert between PDF and formats such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPG and PNG. It works on a phone, tablet or computer — just open your browser and start. Try it here: https://theeditpdf.com If you work with PDFs regularly, I would love to hear which tool you use most, and what would make this more useful for you.

entry.title: Supabase RLS Explained: Policies, Roles, and Common Security Mistakes
entry.summary: Supabase gives the browser a key that talks straight to your database. There is no API server in the middle deciding who gets what, which means your Row Level Security (RLS) policies are your application's actual permission layer. Most tutorials stop at auth.uid() = user_id. Real apps need roles, team tenancy, paid content access, and public pages with private drafts. Every request to the Supabase Data API runs as one of three Postgres roles: anon: No signed-in user. RLS applies. authenticated: A signed-in user's access token is present.
